_comment: Injected bugs (RFC 0035, section 11), checked by scripts/corpus-gate.py --inject and --full:
each patch applies to a copy of its config's pinned checkout, which is built with
weavec-cc in trap mode (the config's `build`, or the entry's own); then `run` executes (the
config's `test` when the entry has none), and the run must stop at `file`:`line`, the line
that carries the INJECTED comment, or at `stop` when the entry names another place (a freed
pointer passed to a function that reads it stops in that function): a run-time report there,
of one of `kinds` when the entry names them. `unlocated` allows a stop that names no line:
`invalid-release`, the allocator refusing a release (a double free), or `fault`, a fault on
the null page (a call through a null function pointer). --inject --reference-only builds each
with ASan and UBSan (with _FORTIFY_SOURCE for `fortify` entries: short writes ASan cannot
see) and checks that `run` reaches the same place.

injections.description: writes the string after sdsfree released its header allocation (s_free of s - header)
frees the token vector twice in sdsfreesplitres
sdsMakeRoomFor frees the old header allocation before copying the string out of it
cJSON_Delete writes the item after freeing it through the global_hooks.deallocate hook
cJSON_Delete frees the value string twice through the deallocate hook; the analysis of the unit alone does not see through the hook, and the runtime's allocator refuses the second release
parse_number terminates its number_string_length + 1 byte copy one byte past the end
cJSONUtils_FindPointerFromObjectTo frees the child path (cJSON_free, defined in cJSON.c) before formatting it
overwrite_item deletes the child tree twice (cJSON_Delete is defined in cJSON.c)
jsondump frees the token array and then dumps it
jsondump's end-of-input cleanup frees the input buffer twice
log_log's callback loop reads one entry past the callback table when all slots are in use
lock() calls the optional lock callback without testing it, which is null unless log_set_lock was called
_ftoa's precision limit is off by one, so a precision of 10 reads pow10[10]
freeHistory clears the first entry of the history array after freeing the array
linenoiseHistorySetMaxLen frees the old history array before copying the entries out of it
example.c reads the line after releasing it with linenoiseFree, defined in linenoise.c
example.c releases the line twice: free, then linenoiseFree from linenoise.c
deflateEnd frees the pending buffer twice through the stream's zfree function pointer
inflateEnd writes the state through its local alias after freeing it with zfree
gzclose_r frees the path through the state after freeing the state
gzclose_w frees the input buffer twice
inflate's code-length loop runs one step too far and reads order[19] for every dynamic block
luaH_free writes the table after luaM_free released it through g->frealloc
luaF_freeproto frees the constant array twice through luaM_freearray (g->frealloc)
a helper in lua.c reads a malloc'd copy of the prompt after freeing it (plain malloc/free)
close_state writes the global state after freeing the main block through g->frealloc
strbuffer_close frees the buffer a second time outside the null test
json_array_remove releases the removed element's reference twice
json_delete_string writes the string after freeing it through jsonp_free
hashtable_do_del releases the pair's value after freeing the pair
do_dump passes snprintf a size one larger than its integer buffer
sdsrange writes one byte past the terminator's byte; for a string with no spare room (alloc == len) that is one past its allocation, which only the runtime knows the size of
sdscatlen reads the string through the pointer it had before sdsMakeRoomFor, which reallocates (and here moves) the header allocation when the string has to grow

parse_string writes a byte two past its terminator, which is one byte past its output allocation (the string's length, its opening quote's byte and the terminator) whenever the string has no escape sequence
print reads the print buffer through buffer->buffer after hooks->reallocate (a function pointer) shrank it, which moves it to a smaller size class
updatewindow writes window[wsize], one byte past the sliding window ZALLOC (a function pointer) returned
inflateEnd reads the sliding window after ZFREE (a function pointer) released it

injections.run: ./lua -e "local function f(n) if n == 0 then return 0 end return 1 + f(n - 1) end assert(f(5000) == 5000)"
injections.description: luaF_newLclosure clears upvals[nupvals], one element past the closure's trailing upvalue array
